svg.title: FastaLake default pipeline
svg.desc: Study-wide exact protein lookup; per-acquisition candidate retrieval, selection parsimony and Sage search; shared study groups, summed intensities and quality control.
svg.text: Protein selection, search and study quantification

g.title: Within each acquisition, retain positive-score predictions of 9–50 residues after the complexity filter, using the top-30% score threshold and retaining ties. Pool distinct I/L-equivalent queries and retrieve complete proteins by exact containment with Aho–Corasick.
g.text: Retrieve complete proteins by exact peptide lookup.
Isoleucine and leucine are treated as equivalent.
9–50 residues · top 30% per run; score ties retained

g.title: Use the same lookup filter on each acquisition’s predictions to retrieve candidates from the study-supported protein space. Lookup uses the entire predicted sequence, with isoleucine and leucine equivalent and no enzyme constraint.

Selection parsimony uses all eligible predictions mapping to the candidates, including those below the lookup score threshold. Fixed unique- and total-evidence counts rank compatible proteins; accession hashes resolve ties. Retain complete proteins receiving evidence. This operation is separate from post-search study grouping.

Sage 0.14.6 searches one acquisition at a time against its selected FASTA. The default is closed tryptic searching over peptides of 5–50 residues, with generated decoys and native label-free intensities. Target peptides pass at peptide q ≤ 0.01 before study grouping. The lookup minimum of nine residues is not a final-identification length filter.

A deterministic greedy cover of the accepted peptide–protein graph defines a single study dictionary, restricted to the FASTAs actually searched. Each canonical peptide is assigned to the first selected representative explaining it. Sum positive finite LFQ feature intensities only where that peptide was accepted in the same acquisition, preserving missing values and counting each admitted feature once.
g.text: Assign accepted peptides to shared study groups;
sum their intensities within each run.

g.title: AlphaPeptTools 0.4.0 reports detection, intensity and missingness without extra normalization or imputation. PCA runs on complete varying groups when at least three nonempty acquisitions and two eligible groups are available; otherwise the output records why it was skipped.
